title: Add Error Handling and Test Cases to an Existing Program
learningObjectives: Describe the purpose and scope of add error handling and test cases to an existing program.
Plan the required data, inputs, outputs, and behaviors.
Break the solution into manageable functions or steps.
Implement and test normal, invalid, and boundary cases.
Review the result and explain limitations and improvements.

understand.concept: Adding error handling means identifying operations that can fail, deciding how failures are represented, handling them at the appropriate level, and giving users a recovery path. Tests should verify both successful outcomes and expected failures, including invalid input, boundaries, and error paths. Error handling should not hide failures or expose sensitive diagnostics.
understand.whyItMatters: Real programs must remain understandable when inputs, files, or operations do not work as expected.
understand.analogy: Think of completing a small real-world task by defining the goal, organizing the work, checking each step, and reviewing the finished result.
understand.analogyLimit: Software projects require precise requirements, data and code design, technical testing, and iterative change; the analogy only introduces a workflow.

explain.narrative:
Adding error handling means identifying operations that can fail, deciding how failures are represented, handling them at the appropriate level, and giving users a recovery path. Tests should verify both successful outcomes and expected failures, including invalid input, boundaries, and error paths. Error handling should not hide failures or expose sensitive diagnostics.

Build incrementally and keep the project scope appropriate for your current skills. The examples illustrate individual design steps; they are not a complete ready-made project. Test your own implementation and document assumptions.

examples.explanation: An explicit outcome lets callers handle failures.

examples.title: Test expected error
examples.explanation: Tests can assert the error result.

examples.title: Test a boundary
examples.explanation: Boundary tests cover values at and around limits.

examples.title: Give recovery guidance
examples.code:
const userMessage='Please enter a whole number from 1 to 5.';
console.log(userMessage);
examples.expectedOutput: Please enter a whole number from 1 to 5.
examples.explanation: Actionable messages help users correct input.

commonMistakes: Starting implementation without defining scope or acceptance criteria.
Combining input, logic, and display in one tangled block.
Claiming features or data persist when they are only in memory.
Adding features before the core workflow works and is tested.

guidedTask.title: Guided Project
guidedTask.instructions: Review a fictional existing program. Add explicit error outcomes for invalid input, missing data, and a failed operation. Write tests for normal behavior, boundaries, and each error path.
steps: Review a fictional existing program. Add explicit error outcomes for invalid input, missing data, and a failed operation. Write tests for normal behavior, boundaries, and each error path.
Write a short scope and acceptance checklist.
Test a normal case and at least two edge/error cases.

independentTask.title: Independent Project
independentTask.instructions: Choose a small program, create a failure-point inventory, add error handling, then write a test table with inputs, expected results, and error messages. Include retest notes.
requirements: Keep the project original and appropriately scoped.
Choose a small program, create a failure-point inventory, add error handling, then write a test table with inputs, expected results, and error messages. Include retest notes.
Include a short test plan and results.
